_note: Banter and everyday chat for #random and #general, built from parts. people[id].obs: [topic, text] about ordinary office life, with slots {yday} {week} {top} {dayname} {month} {weather} (facts of the day). replies[person][topic]: answers that fit the topic. habits: a person's sign-off tics. clauses: a fact of the day tacked on. weather: by month. Banter picks without replacement within a month.

obs.text: The kettle has been on since nine, and I am not ashamed to say it is the heart of this company.
I have bought a new tin of tea. It is on the shelf above the sink, and it is for everyone, even Mr Scrooge.
If the kettle is empty, please do fill it for the next person. It is the oldest rule we have and the best.
I have brought a pie for lunch. It is far too large for one man, and I mean that as an invitation.
Lunch is a sacred thing. Please take a proper hour, and do not eat at your desk if you can help it.
The baker's had a tray of iced buns this morning. I bought six. They will not last, so be quick.
It is a {weather} {dayname}, and I find that a warm room and a good team put right most things.
{weather} out there. Wrap up if you are going to the post box, and borrow my scarf if you need to.
The post has come, and there is a postcard from a customer who says the sock changed her mornings. I have pinned it up.
Another good letter this morning. It makes the work feel worth it, and it is only a Tuesday-sized letter.
We took {yday_n} yesterday. Every one is a person who chose us, and I like to remember that.
I had a kind email from a customer today. I shall not say which, but I read it twice and smiled.
{top} is the favourite this week. Do give it a fond look as you pass the shelf.
It is {dayname}, which is a perfectly good day for doing things properly and going home on time.
I have put a little plant on the windowsill. It looks lonely, so please say good morning to it.
The office is looking very well this {month}. Thank you all for keeping it so tidy.
There is a pile of Spare Socks by the door, waiting to go out. I have never seen a happier pile.
I was down in the stockroom earlier. Mole has made it very neat. I told him so, and he went pink.
We have been at this {month} work a long time now, and I think we are getting rather good at it.
I have a cake in the cupboard. It is not for any occasion. That is the best sort of cake.

habits: That is all. Thank you, everyone.

obs.text: The kettle was left on again. It boiled for twenty minutes and no one drank any of it. I have turned it off.
Tea bags are used once. Twice is a luxury, and thrice is a scandal, but I will not name names.
I have brought bread and cheese. It costs very little, and it tastes of nothing wasted.
Someone bought a pastry from the baker's on the company's tab. I do not say who. I only say I have seen the slip.
It is {weather} today. The heating is on. I should like to see it off by three.
Another {weather} {dayname}. A good day for staying indoors and counting things.
The post has brought two bills and no letters of thanks. That is the usual ratio.
A stamp costs money. Please do not use two when one will do.
Yesterday's orders came to {yday_n}. I have counted them twice, to be sure, which cost nothing.
A customer asked for a free gift. I said the gift was the product. It was not well received.
{top} is selling best this week. It had better, for what it cost us to stock.
The month of {month} is a month like any other. It has the same number of pennies in it.
It is {dayname}. The rent is due and does not care what day it is.
The stockroom light was on at six. A light left on is a coin left on a table.
The new plant on the windowsill costs nothing to feed but water. I have approved it, on those terms.
The Spare Sock sells for seven pounds and costs us far less. I find that a most agreeable fact.
I have found a coat button in the drawer. I have put it in the lost-and-found jar. It may be worth something.
The biscuit tin is lighter than it was on Monday. I have not complained. I have only noticed.
I am sorry to say the kettle is making a noise. I think it wants descaling. I will do it at lunch if no one minds.
I brought in a spare mug in case a visitor comes. It is on the shelf, with a small label.
I have a sandwich from home. It is not one of ours, I'm afraid. I hope that isn't disloyal.
It is a little cold for the walk to the baker's, so I'll eat at my desk. I'll put the crumbs in the bin.
It is {weather} this {dayname} and I did not bring an umbrella. I hope it holds off for the walk home.
I am wearing two jumpers. It is rather {weather} in the corner by the window.
There is a letter for Mr Scrooge in the tray. I've put it where he will see it, but not so he is startled.
The postman wished me a good morning. I do hope I said it back. I believe I did.
I entered {yday_n} for yesterday. I hope I have not made an error. I checked, in any case.
A customer thanked us for a very small thing today. It made my morning in a way I cannot quite explain.
{top} did best this week, according to my sheets. I have underlined it in blue.
It is {dayname}. I have the {month} figures to do, and I am glad of it, in a way.
The clock in the hall says ten past, and my watch says nine past. I am not sure whom to trust.
I went down to the stockroom to ask Mole a question. He had already answered it before I asked, which was kind.
The little plant has a new leaf. I would not like to make a fuss, but it seems to be doing well.
I have counted the Spare Socks on the shelf, and the number is the number it should be. Which is a pleasant thing.
I put the pencils in order this morning. I hope no one minds. They were all lying about.
There was a crumb in the ledger today. I'm sorry. It has been removed with a clean cloth.
The kettle boiled at 9:02. It was ready at 9:03. I record this only because it was exact.
Tea break began at 10:30 and finished at 10:44. A fourteen-minute interval is correct.
Lunch was at 12:00 as scheduled. The sandwich was consumed in nine minutes. I walked for twenty.
The baker's closed at 13:00 sharp. I arrived at 12:58. A close thing, and I do not like close things.
{weather}. The carrier collects at 15:30 and the parcels are at the door by 15:20.
{dayname}: loading took 11 minutes yesterday, which is two more than normal. I have written it down.
The post was delivered at 8:47 today. Yesterday it was 8:52. I am keeping a log.
A parcel came back today with a note on it. It had been to the right house and the wrong door.
Yesterday: {yday_n}. The last parcel left at 15:42. I have written the time in the log.
A customer telephoned to ask when the van would come. I told them the minute. They said that was unusual.
{top} was the most-packed item this week. I can pack it in four minutes.
The hall clock was two minutes slow. I have corrected it. Please do not touch it.
It is {dayname}. The week has seven days and I have used each of them well.
Stockroom shelves were tidy at 8:40. By 8:55 they had been tidied again. Mole is thorough.
The tape gun has been moved. I would like it back at the bench, on the left, at the usual angle.
There are 34 Spare Socks ready for dispatch. I have counted them, and then counted them again.
The plant on the windowsill leans toward the light by about four degrees. I have turned the pot a quarter.
I walked to work in twenty-three minutes today. One minute less than yesterday. I will not explain further.
I made a pot of tea and left it on the table. It is a bit strong. I hope it is all right.
The kettle makes a nice sound when it starts. It is like a small bird. I like that.
I have brought a boiled egg. I peeled it this morning. It is a good egg.
The baker's gave me a bun with too much sugar on it. I have saved a piece for anyone who wants one.
It is {weather} today. I like the sound of it on the roof when I am down in the stockroom.
{weather} this {dayname}. I wore my thick socks. They are not ours. They are my own.
A parcel came back from the carrier today, a bit squashed. I flattened the box and put it in the pile.
The postman's dog came in and sat by the door. He did not want anything. I gave him half a biscuit.
I packed {yday_n} yesterday. It was a good kind of tired.
A customer sent a drawing of the Spare Sock. I have put it on the wall by the shelf, if anyone wants to look.
{top} is on the front shelf this week. I put a little label by it, in pencil.
It is {dayname}. I like {dayname}s. They are not too busy and not too quiet.
I tidied the shelves again. I think I like it best when everything is in its place, even the odd things.
There is a spider behind the tape shelf. She has made a very good web. I have left her to it.
The Spare Sock boxes are stacked in tens. I like them stacked in tens. They look like a little wall.
The little plant on the sill has a new leaf. I gave it some water, but only a bit.
I found a nice mug at the back of the cupboard. I washed it and put it by the kettle.
I always think the afternoon is the loveliest bit, when it goes quiet and the light comes in low.
Whoever is responsible for the state of the kettle knows who they are. I will say no more, this once.
A reminder that the kettle is for everyone and the washing up is for everyone too.
Lunch is at one. I would like everyone to eat something that is not a biscuit.
I have made a stew and brought enough for three. Sam, Esther, that means you.
It is {weather} and I want everyone to have a hot drink before the afternoon queue.
{weather} this {dayname}. Coats on the pegs, not the chairs, please.
The post has come. I have put the customer letters on my desk and the bills on Mr Scrooge's, as is right.
A parcel came back unopened this morning. I have written to the customer, kindly but clearly.
Yesterday we had {yday_n}. The inbox is the length it should be, and I would like it to stay that way.
A customer asked for the manager, then for the manager's manager. They got Mr Fezziwig, who gave them tea.
{top} is the one people are asking about most this week. Sam, Esther, please know the answers.
It is {dayname}. The next meeting is at ten, and it starts at ten.
I would like all desks clear by five on {dayname}. It makes Monday kinder.
I have asked Mole to leave one clear aisle in the stockroom. The boxes had begun to wander.
The Spare Sock page gets a good many questions. I have written the answers down so we say the same thing each time.
The plant on the windowsill is doing better than the rest of us. I have decided to take that as encouragement.
There is a pile of lost-property gloves in my drawer. Claim yours or they go to the charity shop on Friday.
I would like someone to tell me where the good scissors have gone. I will wait.
The kettle is boiling with a noise like a donkey in a tin bath, but it does produce the tea, so I forgive it.
Made tea for the whole office and gave Mr Scrooge the chipped mug. He never notices. It is like a game.
I had a pie for lunch that was as big as a hat. I mean a small hat. Possibly a bonnet.
The baker's pasties are the best thing in the county, and the second-best thing is looking at the baker's pasties.
It is {weather} out there, wet as a haddock's holiday. I came in with half the street on my coat.
A {weather} {dayname}, and a cat on the doorstep looking as miserable as a duck in a dry well.
The post came in a heap as high as a plum duff. I sorted it in a minute and a half and felt very grand.
A parcel came back this morning with 'not known at this address' on it, which is a hard thing to be told about your own address.
{yday_n} yesterday, as busy as a bee in a bonnet shop. Lovely.
A customer asked me whether the Indoor Helmet works outdoors. I told them it works wherever there is a head.
{top} is flying out this week like a pigeon from a pie, and I am glad to see it go.
It is {dayname}, and I feel as lively as a cricket on a hot brick.
My watch has stopped. I have decided it is a sign. Of what, I have not worked out.
Mole has made the stockroom as tidy as a bishop's bedroom. I had to ask him where anything was.
The Spare Sock pile by the door has grown like a mushroom. A very tidy mushroom, mind.
The windowsill plant is a handsome thing, taller than it was and prouder than it ought to be.
I could eat a horse. I won't, but I could. A sandwich will do, if it is one of ours.
I saw a postman with a moustache like a hairbrush. I felt he deserved a mention.
I hope nobody minds, but I have descaled the kettle. It looked a bit tired.
I made tea for the queue and left a cup on Mrs Hudson's desk. I hope that is all right.
I brought a small salad. It is rather plain. I hope it does not smell of onions.
Thank you to whoever left the bun on my desk. I do not know who it was, but it was very kind.
It is {weather} today. I hope everyone got in without too much trouble.
{weather} this {dayname}. I'm told it may be better by the weekend, although I always hope for too much.
A letter came for me in the post, which was a surprise. It was from a customer who had written a thank-you.
A parcel came back to us today. I hope the customer is all right. I've put a note on the case.
Yesterday there were {yday_n}, so the queue is a little longer than usual. I'm managing, I think.
A customer was very nice to me on the phone today. I'm not used to it, but I enjoyed it.
{top} has had the most questions this week. I have started a small list of the answers.
It is {dayname}. I feel I have not quite got the week yet, but I am trying.
I took a box down to the stockroom and Mole took it from me before I could say anything. He is very helpful.
I have been reading about the Spare Sock. It is more thoughtful than I had thought.
I watered the windowsill plant. I hope I did not give it too much.
Someone left a flask in the kitchen. It is blue. If it is yours, it is on the second shelf.
I stayed late on Tuesday, and I noticed how quiet the office is in the evening. I rather liked it.
I'm sorry to be a bother, but has anyone seen the stapler? I'm sure I had it a minute ago.
Kettle supplies, as of this morning: tea, 40 bags; milk, one pint; sugar, half a bag. I have written it on the list.
We are low on mugs. I have put two on my list, to be bought in the next order.
Supplies for lunch: bread, cheese, two apples. I plan ahead. It is a habit from long ago.
I have put aside a loaf for the week. It is wrapped in a cloth. Please do not use the end.
It is {weather} today. I have checked the roof for leaks, and there is one, small, which I have marked.
{weather} {dayname}. The stockroom door needs a better seal. I have added it to the list.
The post brought a catalogue of tape. I have read it with great interest and marked three items.
A parcel came back. I have put it on the shelf with a label, so we know what it is and where it was.
Yesterday's {yday_n} will want replacing on the shelves, and I have a list for it.
A customer asked for a spare part we do not make. I have written it down, in case we should.
{top} is the best-seller this week. I have checked how many we have left, and written down the number.
It is {dayname}. I make a list of what to buy every {dayname}, and today's list is a long one.
I have inspected the stockroom shelves and made a list of what is running low. It has eleven items.
Spare tape, spare labels, spare string. Always have spare string. That is my rule.
The Spare Sock is the one product I never worry about. It is small, it keeps, and it always sells.
The plant on the windowsill needs a bigger pot. I have added a pot to the list.
I have written down everything I need before winter: boxes, tape, a stove, candles. I like to be ready.
If the van breaks down, I know where we can find a spare. I always know where the spare is.
I have had the most wonderful idea about the kettle. I will tell you when I have worked out what it is.
Could we get a kettle that plays a tune when it boils? I think it would be marvellous for morale.
I've read about a new kind of lunch box and I think it will change everything. I'll bring one in.
Anyone want to try a new sandwich filling I invented in the shower? It involves pickles. Possibly jam.
It is {weather} today, which is exactly the right weather for a new project. I have several.
{weather} {dayname}! I think it would be a splendid day for a photograph of the Spare Sock in the rain.
The post has brought a magazine about kites. I've read it from cover to cover and I'm going to learn.
A parcel came back to us with a lovely stamp on it. I have taken a photograph. It might make a post.
We had {yday_n} yesterday! Imagine if it was double! I have a plan for double.
A customer wrote us a poem about the Spare Sock. It rhymes. I'm having it framed.
{top} is the star this week. I'm thinking of a small film about it. Perhaps a very small film.
It is {dayname}, and I feel a new craze coming on. I won't say which until I know.
I woke up with an idea about a newsletter. Then I lost it. It will come back. They always do.
I went to the stockroom and photographed the shelves. They look like art, but with boxes.
I think the Spare Sock deserves its own theme tune. Does anyone play the accordion?
I have bought a second plant for the windowsill. I think we are building a small jungle. Possibly a pocket one.
I've decided I'm going to learn juggling. I've bought three oranges. Two are already gone.
I am in the middle of reading about a craze for pressing flowers. I think we should do something. I don't know what.
Mended a kettle. Not ours. Someone left it on the bench with a note.
Kettle is fine. I checked the element.
Lunch at the bench. Sandwich. Quiet.
The baker's pasty is good. I do not say that often.
{weather}. The workshop stays warm. I like that.
{dayname}, {weather}. Window handle is loose again. I'll tighten it.
A parcel came back with a dent. Not a fault. Just a dent.
Post brought a part I was waiting for. Good.
Yesterday: {yday_n}. Few returns. Good.
A customer sent a photo of a repair. It was not ours, but the repair was neat.
{top} is the one I see most on the bench this week. It is a sound design.
It is {dayname}. The bench is clear. I will find something to take apart.
Stockroom shelf had a loose bracket. Fixed it. Took four minutes.
Spare Sock needs no repair. Hard to improve.
The plant on the sill is fine. It needs nothing. I admire that.
Solder smells like a good morning. I do not say that to everyone.
Biscuit tin is empty. I did not do it. I have a witness. The witness is a spider.

kettle: Quite so. It is a good kettle.
Thank you for looking after it.
Splendid. The kettle deserves it.
lunch: A good lunch is half the afternoon. Do take your time.
That sounds delightful. Please save me a corner.
Capital. I will join you, if there is room at the table.
weather: So it is. A warm room puts most things right.
Quite so. Do look after yourselves.
Indeed. Thank you for mentioning it.
post: Thank you for sorting it. I'll read the letters after lunch, with a cup of tea.
A good letter makes the whole day. Please do put it on the wall.
Splendid. Leave it on my desk, and I'll write back myself.
customer: That is a fine thing to hear. Thank you for telling us.
Our customers are very good to us. We must be good to them.
Wonderful. A little kindness goes a long way, in both directions.
products: That is the sort of news I like. Thank you.
Good, good. And a small cheer for everyone who made it.
Quite so. Thank you for telling us.
clock: Quite right. We have time for a decent day's work and a decent evening.
A good rule. I shall keep it.
Indeed. No need to hurry what can be done properly.
stockroom: Mole does it beautifully. Please tell him I said so.
A tidy stockroom is a happy stockroom. Thank you all.
That is good to hear. I shall go down and have a look.
sock: The sock is a fine thing. We should be proud of it.
Splendid. One sock, thought through. It is a small triumph.
Very good. I'll have a look at them on my way out.
plants: I am so pleased. We shall have a forest by spring, if this continues.
A little green does everyone good. Thank you.
Lovely. I'll bring in a second one, if there is room.
returned_parcel: Poor parcel. Please make sure the customer is looked after, whatever it cost.
Thank you. Do be kind to the customer when you write.
A pity. Let us see that it is put right.

kettle: I'll keep an eye on it, if I may.
Thank you. I'll mention it to anyone who asks.
I hope that is all right.
lunch: That sounds very nice. I'm sorry, I did not bring enough to share.
Thank you for saying. I'll make sure to take a proper break.
I'll join you, if I am not in the way.
weather: I noticed that on the way in, I'm afraid.
post: Thank you for sorting it. I'll put the bills in the tray, as usual.
I hope the letter is a kind one. I'll leave it where it can be seen.
customer: That is very good. I have written the figure in the book, I hope correctly.
Thank you. I hope the customers keep on being so kind.
I'm glad. It is a comfort to have good news in the figures.
products: I'll note that on my sheets. Thank you.
That is useful to know. I will underline it.
I hope I have recorded the numbers right. I'll check them again.
clock: Thank you. I'll be sure to leave on time, if I can.
I'm sorry, I lost track of the day. Thank you for reminding me.
That is a good rule. I shall try to follow it.
stockroom: I'm sorry to hear it, and glad it is being seen to.
Thank you, Mole. I do appreciate how tidy it is.
I'll make a note of it, if that helps.
sock: A small triumph. I rather like them.
Thank you. I'll put it in the figures.
Thank you. I'll make a note of it, if that helps.
plants: It does look better than it did. I'm glad.
Thank you. I'll make a note of it, if that helps.
I hope that's all right.
returned_parcel: I'm sorry to hear it. I'll note it in the books if it needs a refund.
Thank you for telling me. I hope the customer is not too put out.
I'll check the order, if that helps.

kettle: That's nice.
I'll remember that.
Thank you for telling me.
lunch: Thank you. I'll sit by the window and have mine.
That's nice.
Thank you for telling me.
post: I hope the letter was nice. It sounds nice.
customer: I'm glad. I like to think of someone opening a box and being pleased.
That's a nice thing. Thank you for telling me.
That's nice.
products: I'll put it at the front. I'll put it where it can be seen.
That's good. I'll make sure there are enough in the boxes.
That's nice.
clock: Thank you. I'll be on time, or a minute early, which is the same thing.
I like {dayname}s, too.
That sounds right. I'll go with that.
stockroom: I'm sorry if I made a mess. I tidied it again just now.
Thank you. I do like it neat.
That's nice.
sock: That's nice.
Thank you for telling me.
I'll remember that.
plants: It does look happy. I think it likes the window.
That's nice.
Thank you for telling me.
returned_parcel: I'll find a new box for it, if it is going out again.
Poor thing. I'll put it by the packing bench.
I'll look at it, in case it can be mended.

kettle: Noted. Please do not leave it to someone else.
Thank you. The kettle is everyone's responsibility.
I will see to it, if no one else does.
lunch: Good. Please eat properly and take a full break.
Thank you. I will hold you to it.
Sit down for it, please. Not at the desk.
weather: Thank you. We carry on regardless.
post: Thank you. I will take the customer letters. You take the bills.
I will answer it today. Thank you for flagging.
customer: I will pick that up. Do not worry.
That is good. Keep it up, and keep it polite.
Noted. Thank you.
products: Noted. Thank you.
Quite so. Carry on.
Thank you. I'll bear it in mind.
clock: Quite right. We'll start on time.
I'll hold you to that.
Noted. Thank you.
stockroom: Good. I would like it to stay that way.
I'll take a look at it this afternoon.
Noted. Thank you.
sock: Noted. That's a good sign.
I'd like them packed well. Customers notice.
Noted. Thank you.
plants: It does help. Thank you for looking after it.
Noted. Thank you.
Quite so. Carry on.
returned_parcel: Thank you. Please add a note to the case, and I will write to the customer.
I will deal with it. Please leave the paperwork on my desk.
Noted. Let me know what the carrier says.

kettle: Bless that kettle, it's the busiest thing in the building.
Fair play to the kettle.
I'll drink to that, in a manner of speaking.
lunch: That sounds as good as a Christmas goose. Save me a bit!
I'm there before you can say knife and fork.
Lunch is the best bit of the day, bar the bit after it.
weather: Weather's a funny customer, as the umbrella said to the hat.
Right you are, and no mistake.
I'd noticed, as keen as a weathercock.
post: Right as a trivet. I'll sort the rest, as quick as a wink.
I do like a post day, it's like Christmas for grown-ups.
That's a good letter. I'll read it twice, once for me and once for the dog.
customer: Lovely stuff! That's what we're here for, as the vicar said to the churchwarden.
Bless them, they're all as good as gold. Well, most of them.
Right you are, as the fiddler said to the dancer.
products: That's the way, like a duck takes to water.
Selling like hot buns at a fair, it is.
I'll tell the next person who asks. Nice and firm.
clock: Time flies like an arrow, and fruit flies like a banana.
I'm as spry as a spring lamb today.
A good day for it, as they say.
stockroom: Tidier than a bishop's bedroom, that is. I'm impressed.
Mole's the man for the job, as neat as a new pin.
I'll go and have a look, and try not to move anything.
sock: Happy as a sandboy, that pile. Pat it on the head for me.
A sock a day keeps the cold away, as nobody says.
I've a soft spot for the Spare Sock. It's the quiet hero of the shop.
plants: Green as a gooseberry, and prouder than a peacock.
I'll give it a little talking-to. Plants like to be encouraged.
A handsome thing, that. Better-looking than the lot of us.
returned_parcel: Back like a boomerang, bless it. I'll write to them kindly.
Poor parcel, home again with its tail between its legs.
I'll chase the carrier. I'm as keen as a bloodhound on this one.

kettle: Thank you for letting us know.
I'll look after it too, if that helps.
That is kind.
lunch: That sounds lovely. I hope I'm not in the way if I sit nearby.
Thank you. I'll make sure to have a proper break.
Thank you for telling us.
post: Thank you. I'll sort the rest, if that helps.
I hope the letter was a kind one. I'll keep an eye out.
customer: Thank you. I'm glad it went well.
Thank you for telling us.
I'm glad you said.
products: That is useful. I'll mention it to the next person who writes.
I'll check the page, in case it needs a note.
Thank you for telling us.
clock: I'll try to keep pace. Thank you.
I hope I have not been too slow. I'll do better.
That is a good way of looking at it.
stockroom: Thank you, Mole. I'd have been lost without you.
I'm sorry if I got in the way. I'll try not to next time.
Thank you for telling us.
sock: It is a thoughtful little thing, isn't it? I've grown fond of it.
I like it more than I thought I would.
Thank you for telling us.
plants: I'm glad it is doing well. I think it likes you.
Thank you for telling us.
I'm glad you said.
returned_parcel: I'll check whether the customer has written in. I hope it is nothing serious.
Thank you. I'll keep an eye on the case.
I'll write to them, if that would help.

kettle: Brilliant! The kettle is the heart of the office!
I love the kettle! It has presence!
Yes! May I photograph it?
lunch: That sounds marvellous! May I take a picture of it?
Brilliant! Absolutely brilliant!
Yes! I love it!
weather: Weather! It makes everything more dramatic!
I love weather! It is good for photographs!
Yes! I shall take a picture from the window!
post: A post-day post! That's an idea. Possibly a good one!
Can I photograph the letter? With permission, of course!
How marvellous! I'll put it on the board for everyone!
customer: This is exactly what we need! May I use it in a post, with permission?
That's wonderful! I have eleven ideas, but I'll tell you only one!
Brilliant! Absolutely brilliant!
products: Yes! A film! Or a small book! Or a song! Possibly all three!
Brilliant! I'll put it in the next post! Possibly two!
